title: Decision transformer: returns-to-go, causal masking, and conditioning on a return
brief: Compute returns-to-go, lay out (return, state, action) tokens, build and test a causal mask, roll out a target return, and see what conditioning on a return cannot do.
hints: returns_to_go runs backward: running = rewards[t] + gamma * running, then store running at t. Storing before you add r_t leaves the reward at t out of entry t.
build_tokens returns three arrays, kinds, timesteps, and values. Loop over steps, and append the action token only when t < len(actions).
causal_mask is np.tril(np.ones((n, n), dtype=bool)). With k=1 the state token could read the action it must predict.
masked_attention: scores = q @ k.T / sqrt(d_head), then np.where(mask, scores, -np.inf), subtract the row maximum, exponentiate, and divide by the row sum.
rollout_with_target appends the current target before calling act, so act sees t + 1 targets and t actions. After mdp.step, set the target to (target - r) / gamma.
conditional_action_probs: select samples with np.isclose(returns, target), count their actions with np.bincount(minlength=n_actions), and divide by the number selected.

offline_q_iteration: keep a dict from (s, a) to its transitions, start those entries at 0, and back up r + gamma * Q[s2].max() on each sweep, with no next-state term when done is true. Unseen entries stay at -inf, so they never win the max.
